body:
## Why

`event_id` is `<yyyy-mm>-<series slug>` using the end date's month (`design/data-model.md`). The registry records each occurrence by series and month, believed to be the month results were reported (**unverified**). `design/backfill.md` seeds month-precision events from registry occurrences for 2010 on, so when the two months differ the same edition appears twice, one month apart. The design opens an `event_alias` finding for adjacent-month slug matches rather than merging automatically, pending this measurement.

## Task

- [ ] After the bootstrap sweep completes (#10), join registry occurrences to dated events (calendar and platform rows) by series slug and count exact-month matches, adjacent-month matches, and larger offsets, per year.
- [ ] Record the numbers in a `research/` note with the script that computes them.
- [ ] Decide: if adjacent-month offsets are common, make the merge automatic and record it in `design/backfill.md` ("Event enumeration for history") and the decision log; otherwise keep the finding-plus-override path and remove the **unverified** marker in `design/data-model.md`.

## Done when

The research note exists, the design states the rule with the measured rate, and the marker is gone. Blocks the close of WP12.
title: Measure how often the registry month differs from an event's end-date month

## Why

The Wayback Machine holds EEPro results only from 2018 (148 slugs, `research/wayback-coverage-2026-09-11.md`). The origin still serves older slug directories (`https://eepro.com/results/liberty2018/` returned a 200 index page on 2026-09-11), but `event.php` lists only 2024 on and year indexes (`/results/<year>/`) are 404. `design/backfill.md` rules out learning old slugs by probing: they come from the operator, who is a friend of the owner and has said an API is planned.

## Task

- [ ] Ask the operator for the list of result directories older than 2018 that are still online (or whether the planned API will expose history), and whether they prefer we read them from the origin at one event per cycle with conditional GETs, or wait for the API.
- [ ] Record the date and answer in `docs/sources/eepro.md` section 1 and section 10, and drop the open item in section 13.
- [ ] Turn the answer into `overrides/source_urls.csv` rows or an adapter change, per `design/backfill.md` ("Origin fallback for gaps").

## Done when

The EEPro playbook says which years the origin holds and how we may read them, or that we wait for the API. Part of WP16.
title: Ask the EEPro operator which pre-2018 result slugs still exist

body:
## Why

`design/backfill.md` reads history from 2010-01-01 through the Wayback Machine. The Internet Archive's terms page (`https://archive.org/about/terms`) needs JavaScript, so the pipeline's polite fetch on 2026-09-11 could not read it (`research/verification/2026-09-11/archive_org_terms.hdr`, a 302 to a JS-rendered page). The commonly quoted clause that access is granted for scholarship and research purposes is marked **unverified** in the design.

## Task

- [ ] Read the terms in a browser and note any clause on automated access, rate, or permitted use.
- [ ] Record the date read and the outcome in `docs/sources/wayback-machine.md` section 1, and remove the **unverified** marker in `design/backfill.md` and `design/ethics-and-legal.md` if the wording is confirmed.
- [ ] If the terms restrict our use, decide the change (slower settings, narrower scope, or stop) and record it in the playbook and the decision log.

## Done when

The playbook's status section names the date and what the terms say, and the design no longer marks the clause unverified. Blocks WP11 (`design/backfill.md`, "Work packages").
title: Read the Internet Archive terms before Wayback backfill starts

Found while investigating Lynne Yun (WSDC 26843). Reviewed code `2089803d379ef4233ee45a49193ce97befcf0911`; published baseline `ec6b7bbb84be9e5252d55c6bb1eae3feef05dd5b`.

Her record was absent from the partial registry mirror (sweep cursor 3297). A normal gated lookup succeeded: snapshot `snap_20260911T041431Z_9ae4a83cd7c2`, SHA-256 `9ae4a83cd7c24315e0768edb08d269a85fc7bca3f3964d3c7b1a0ba29273c11d`. It identifies Lynne Yun, 26843, primary follower, required/allowed Novice, 7 points. The body parses and projects successfully.

Her registry has three rows: Swustlicious October 2025, result 4, four points; SASS Spooky Albany Swing Spectacular October 2025, result F, one point; The Boston Tea Party March 2026, result F, two points.

Only Swustlicious maps to a canonical event. `project/registry_events.py` requires an exact normalized name and month; canonical names `SASS` and `Boston Tea Party` do not match the other registry names. The mapper currently has no reviewed registry alias input. Consequently those two results cannot confirm her identities through registry event evidence.

A second distinction remains even after event matching: `_update_registry_points` requires registry.result == str(placement.place). Registry `F` is a finalist category, not the detailed source's 7th place. Do not replace F with an invented rank or broadly relax the exact evidence requirement.

- [ ] Add a reviewed, auditable registry event-alias mechanism with edition/month and ambiguity checks.
- [ ] Establish and document safe handling of a registry finalist category versus a detailed numerical final place; keep raw F intact.
- [ ] Reconcile the SASS and Boston examples with fixtures and provenance, withholding ambiguous point attachments.
- [ ] Replay affected registry links/points and verify no unsupported points attach.
title: Reconcile registry event aliases and preserve finalist point evidence

Found while investigating Lynne Yun (WSDC 26843). Reviewed code `2089803d379ef4233ee45a49193ce97befcf0911`; published baseline `ec6b7bbb84be9e5252d55c6bb1eae3feef05dd5b`.

Her record was absent from the partial registry mirror (sweep cursor 3297). A normal gated lookup succeeded: snapshot `snap_20260911T041431Z_9ae4a83cd7c2`, SHA-256 `9ae4a83cd7c24315e0768edb08d269a85fc7bca3f3964d3c7b1a0ba29273c11d`. It identifies Lynne Yun, 26843, primary follower, required/allowed Novice, 7 points. The body parses and projects successfully.

Local replay reveals false individual associations once this missing dancer enters the mirror:

- `2026-02-swing-crush/hi-lo-j-j-hi-lead-lo-follow/L-291`: name `Gabi Wasserman and Lynne Yun`, role `leader` -> wsdc_id 26843, probable, score 0.9000000000000001.
- `2026-06-jack-jill-o-rama/all-american-60s-era-j-j/L-22`: name `Ben McHenry and Lynne Yun`, role `leader` -> same incorrect individual assignment.

`generate_candidates` uses token-set similarity, so a single dancer contained in a two-person string gets similarity 1.0. Role mismatch is merely a small score reduction; `division=none` matches the dancer's inactive leader level, producing a publishable 0.9 score. The earlier source projection retained a paired name under a leader entry; neither layer protects individual identity ownership.

- [ ] Preserve pair ownership explicitly when a source cell contains both names; infer individual role only from adequate source evidence.
- [ ] Prevent a mixed-person name from becoming a probable/confirmed individual solely through token-set containment.
- [ ] Retain legitimate compound individual names and explicit individual source-ID evidence with suitable regression cases.
- [ ] Review existing mixed-name entries for false links and issue findings where role attribution remains unresolved.
- [ ] Bump affected parser/projector/linker versions, replay, and inspect the published changes.

The two false associations above are from an isolated replay, not a reviewed public release. The newly fetched registry snapshot is queued in production for normal processing; this is a general defect beyond Lynne.
title: Prevent paired source names from linking to the wrong individual role

It identifies Lynne Yun, 26843, primary follower, required/allowed Novice, 7 points. The body parses and projects successfully.

After importing this real registry record into a local copy and replaying 14 events, 15 of 19 individual-name entries link (14 probable, one registry-confirmed), but four remain unmatched despite exact names.

`link/candidates.py:_division_ok` includes `none` as numeric level 0. Non-level contests with `division=none` are therefore deemed incompatible with a Novice follower. `link/score.py` reduces the exact-name score to 0.08; assignment requires 0.5. Reproduced for:

- Atlanta Swing Classic 2025 ProAm New-Nov follower, bib 940.
- Northeast Swing Classic 2025 ProAm New/Nov follower, bib 175.
- MADjam 2026 ProAm New/Nov follower, bib 975.
- SASS 2025 Spooky All American follower, bib 110.

- [ ] Distinguish an unrestricted/unspecified contest division from an actual eligibility level; omit unsupported eligibility evidence instead of treating it as level zero.
- [ ] Preserve rejection of genuine known division mismatches and appropriate handling of unknown dancer levels.
- [ ] Add regression cases using the captured registry evidence and these non-level contest shapes.
- [ ] Bump linker version, replay, review identity changes, and publish verified corrections.

Scope is identity eligibility; do not invent a Novice classification for the source contests.
title: Fix identity eligibility for unrestricted contest divisions
